transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I feel like I’m not handling things the way I should be. I tried to take my art more seriously and turn it into an actual freelance business, and I thought that would be exciting, but lately it’s like every little practical part of it just sends me into a spiral. Like invoices, client messages, following up on things — I get so wound up about them that I end up avoiding them, and then the avoiding makes everything worse.

I’ll sit there knowing I need to reply to someone or send an invoice, and instead I just freeze or put it off, and then later I’m crying at my kitchen table because it feels like I’ve ruined everything or I can’t keep up. And it’s embarrassing because these aren’t huge emergencies, they’re normal things adults deal with. But then I also start forgetting other normal stuff, like paying a bill, because I’m so wrapped up in stressing about the business side of things. So… yeah, I think I came in because this is starting to feel like more than just being busy or disorganized.
Do you find yourself having repetitive, intrusive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that way exactly. I do get stuck thinking about things, like replaying what I should do or what I might have messed up, but I don’t know if they’re “intrusive” in the way you mean. It’s more like once something is stressing me out, my brain keeps circling it and I have a hard time letting it go.

But I haven’t really noticed, like, random thoughts popping into my head that feel completely unwanted or bizarre or anything like that. It’s more connected to whatever I’m already worried about, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or tasks because they make you feel anxious or uncomfortable?

Yes, definitely. That’s actually one of the main reasons I came in. Since I started trying to make my art into a real freelance business, I keep avoiding the exact things that are supposed to make it function — invoices, client messages, following up with people, that kind of thing.

It’s not that I don’t care. I care too much, maybe, or I get so wound up that even opening an email feels like I’m about to find out I’ve done something wrong. So I’ll tell myself, “I’ll do it after lunch,” or “I just need to be in a better headspace,” and then suddenly it’s the next day or the next week, and I feel even worse because now I actually am behind.

And then it turns into this whole thing where I’m sitting at my kitchen table crying over an invoice, which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, but in the moment it feels huge. And because I’m so focused on avoiding or dreading those business tasks, I start dropping normal life stuff too, like forgetting to pay a bill. So yes, I do avoid things when they make me anxious, and then the avoidance kind of makes everything snowball.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform specific rituals or behaviors to reduce your anxiety or stress?

I don’t think so… not in the way I understand rituals, at least. Like, I don’t have something where I have to tap things a certain number of times or check the stove over and over before I can calm down, or anything like that.

I mean, I do procrastinate in these weird little ways, like I’ll tell myself I need to make tea first, or organize the desk, or reread the client’s message a bunch before replying, but that feels more like stalling because I’m anxious, not like a ritual I believe I have to do to keep something bad from happening. It’s more avoidance than a specific behavior that reduces the stress. Honestly, most of the time those little “preparing myself” things don’t reduce it much anyway — they just delay the thing I’m scared to start.

So… no, I haven’t noticed anything that feels like a required ritual. It’s more that I freeze or put things off.
Are there any specific things, like places, objects, or types of social interactions, that make you feel anxious?

Yeah… it’s mostly certain types of interactions, I think. Not so much a place or an object by itself, but anything connected to the freelance business side of my art. Like invoices, client messages, follow-ups — even just seeing an email from someone I’ve done work for can make me tense up.

It sounds small, but it feels like the second I open it, I’m going to find out I forgot something, or did something wrong, or that I’m behind. So I avoid it, and then of course avoiding it makes it worse. I’ll put off sending an invoice or replying to a client until it becomes this huge thing in my head, and then I’m sitting at my kitchen table crying over something that probably would’ve taken ten minutes if I’d just done it earlier.

And it kind of spills over, too. When I’m that wound up about those work-type tasks, I start forgetting normal responsibilities, like paying a bill, because my brain is just stuck on the thing I’m avoiding. So I guess the specific trigger is anything that makes me feel like I have to prove I’m a “real” professional or handle the business part properly. That’s when I get anxious.
Is there anything else in your life, outside of your freelance business, that makes you feel anxious or worried?

Um… outside of the freelance stuff, I’m not sure there’s anything that stands out in the same way. I mean, normal life things can stress me out, like anyone, but I don’t think I have another specific area where I’m consistently anxious or worried.

It’s more that when the business-related things start piling up, they sort of bleed into everything else and make me feel on edge generally. But if you’re asking whether there’s another separate trigger — like family, social situations, being out in public, or something like that — I haven’t really noticed one. The freelance/business side is the thing that feels most tied to the anxiety.
Do you feel a strong need to repeat certain actions or check things over and over when you're feeling anxious?

Not really, no. I mean… when I’m anxious I might reread something a few times, like an email or a message, but it doesn’t feel like I’m compelled to check it over and over in a specific way. It’s more like I’m nervous I’m misunderstanding it or I’m trying to work up the nerve to respond.

I don’t have a thing where I need to repeat an action until it feels “right,” if that makes sense. I’m not checking locks or appliances repeatedly, or doing a certain routine to calm myself down. It’s more that I get stuck hesitating, and then I avoid the thing. So I might look at something, close it, come back to it, overthink it, but it feels like anxiety and procrastination rather than a need to repeat or check.
Do you worry about a wide range of things in your daily life, or is your worrying mostly focused on your freelance business?

It’s mostly focused on the freelance business, yeah. I don’t feel like I’m sitting around worrying about every possible thing in my daily life equally. It really started to become a problem when I tried to make my art into more of a real freelance business, with clients and invoices and messages and all the follow-through that comes with that.

That’s the stuff that gets me wound up. Like, I’ll see a client email or realize I need to send an invoice, and my chest just kind of tightens because I’m immediately thinking I’ve done something wrong or I’m behind or I’m going to look unprofessional. Then I avoid it, and it snowballs until I’m crying at the kitchen table over something that probably wasn’t even that big to begin with.

And then once I’m in that state, it can make me forget regular things, like paying a bill, but I don’t think the bill itself is usually the original worry. It’s more like my brain is so stuck on the freelance stuff that normal responsibilities start slipping too. So, no, I wouldn’t say it’s a wide range of worries all the time — it’s mainly that business side of my art.
Do you think your anxiety would significantly decrease if you were able to find a way to manage or resolve the stresses related to your freelance business?

Yeah, I think it probably would. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like my whole life would magically become perfect, but the anxiety I came in about feels really tied to that specific situation.

Ever since I tried to make my art into an actual freelance business — not just making things, but dealing with clients, invoices, messages, deadlines, all the “professional” parts — that’s when I started getting so wound up. Like I’ll see an email from a client or know I need to send an invoice, and instead of just doing it, I freeze and overthink it, and then I avoid it. And then the avoiding makes it worse, because suddenly it’s been days and now I’m convinced I’ve messed everything up.

So yeah, if I had a way to manage that part better — like not letting the invoices and messages turn into this huge scary thing — I think my anxiety would decrease a lot. Because it’s not like I’m anxious about everything equally. It’s more that this one area gets so overwhelming that it spills over, and then I’m crying at my kitchen table or forgetting basic normal things like paying a bill because I’m so stuck on what I haven’t dealt with for the business.
Is there anything else in your life, outside of your freelance business and the tasks associated with it, that you worry about as much or more than you worry about your business?

No, not really as much as that. I mean, I worry about normal life things sometimes, but nothing grabs me the way the business stuff does.

That’s honestly why I came in — because since I tried to turn my art into a real freelance thing, I keep getting so wound up over the parts that feel “official,” like invoices and client messages. I’ll know I need to answer someone or send something, and instead of just doing it, I get stuck, and then I avoid it, and then it becomes this whole spiral where I’m crying at my kitchen table over it.

And then it starts affecting other things too, like I’ll forget normal responsibilities, like paying a bill, because I’m so tangled up in what I haven’t done for the business. But the main worry is still that. I can’t think of anything outside of it that I worry about as much or more.
Do you think your anxiety started right after you began your freelance business, or was there a period of time where you were able to manage the business side of things without feeling overwhelmed?

There was a little bit of a gap, I think. It didn’t happen the exact day I said, “Okay, I’m doing freelance now.” At first I could kind of convince myself I was just figuring things out, and it felt manageable enough.

The part where I really started getting overwhelmed and avoidant was about a month after I took on the community arts contract and tried to make the business more formal. That’s when it stopped feeling like just making art or doing a few side jobs and started feeling like there were all these official responsibilities attached to it. And I think that shift really got to me.

So, yeah, there was maybe a short period where I was managing, or at least telling myself I was managing. But about a month into that more formal setup, that’s when I noticed I was freezing up and avoiding things instead of just handling them.
Are there any objects or situations, outside of your freelance business, that trigger your anxiety?

Not that I’ve noticed, no. I mean, I can get stressed by normal things like anyone, but I don’t have some other object or situation where I’m like, “Oh, that always sets me off,” outside of the business stuff.

It’s more specific than that, I think. Like it’s not crowds or driving or being in public or anything like that. I haven’t really noticed a pattern where some random situation triggers the same kind of anxiety. The things that make me freeze up are really tied to the freelance side — the responsibility, the official-feeling tasks, that sort of thing.

So… no, I don’t think there’s anything separate from that. At least nothing I can point to.
Do you think your anxiety would decrease if you no longer had to deal with the business side of your freelance work?

I think it probably would, yes, but I don’t really know for sure because I haven’t had that situation yet. The contract is still going, and all the business changes are still kind of… active, I guess. I’m still in the middle of it, so I haven’t had some clean stretch where the stressful part ended and then months went by and I could see, like, “Oh, okay, I’m calmer now.”

So my guess is that if I didn’t have to deal with the business side — the official responsibilities and all of that — I’d feel a lot less wound up. But it’s hard to separate because it hasn’t really stopped. There hasn’t been a point where the stressor, or even the fallout from it, has been over for long enough for me to compare.
Do you think you would still experience significant anxiety if you were to stop your freelance business and no longer have to deal with its related tasks and responsibilities?

I honestly don’t know for sure. I mean, my instinct is to say yes, I’d probably be much less anxious if I stopped doing the freelance business and didn’t have to deal with all those tasks and responsibilities anymore. But the hard part is that I haven’t actually had that happen yet, so I don’t have anything real to compare it to.

The contract is still going, and the business changes are still kind of in motion, so I’m still living inside the thing that’s been stressing me out. There hasn’t been, like, a clean break where it all ended and then a few months passed and I could see whether I settled down or whether the anxiety stayed. Even the fallout from it hasn’t really been over for any length of time.

So I guess my answer is… I suspect I wouldn’t have the same level of anxiety if all of that stopped, but I can’t say with confidence because I haven’t had a stretch where the stressor was actually gone for months.
Do you think your anxiety would completely go away if the stressors related to your freelance business were removed or resolved?

I don’t know that I can say “completely,” honestly. I’d like to think it would go way down, because so much of it seems tied to the freelance business stuff, but I haven’t really had a chance to test that.

The contract is still going, and the business changes are still happening, so I’m still sort of in the middle of the thing. It’s not like everything got resolved and then I had a few calm months afterward to see whether I actually felt normal again. Even the aftermath hasn’t really had time to settle, if that makes sense.

So… maybe it would mostly go away, but I can’t confidently say it would completely disappear, because I haven’t had that stretch where the stressor and all the fallout from it were actually over for months.
Do you believe you would experience no anxiety at all if you were no longer involved in your freelance business?

I don’t think I can honestly say “no anxiety at all.” That feels too absolute. I mean, I can imagine it would be less if I wasn’t involved in the freelance business anymore, because that’s where so much of the pressure has been coming from. But I haven’t really had the chance to see what I’m like without it.

The contract is still going, and the business changes are still happening, so it’s not like I’ve had this clear period where everything ended and then, say, a few months went by and I could tell whether the anxiety fully disappeared or just eased up. Even the fallout from it hasn’t really been over long enough to know.

So I guess I’d say I hope I’d feel a lot calmer, but I wouldn’t want to claim I’d have no anxiety at all, because I just don’t have that stretch of time to compare it to.
Do you think you would still worry about other things in your life if your freelance business and its related stresses were completely resolved?

I think I probably would still worry about some things, just because life has other things in it, but I don’t really know how much of that would be normal everyday worry versus this same kind of anxiety I’ve been feeling.

The frustrating part is that I don’t have a clean example to look at. The contract is still going, and the business changes are still happening, so I haven’t had, like, a real stretch of time where the stressor was gone and even the fallout from it had been over for months. I’m still sort of in the middle of it, so it’s hard for me to separate what’s “me worrying about other things” from what’s just the business stress bleeding into everything.

So I guess my honest answer is yes, maybe I’d still worry about other things, but I can’t really tell how much until this whole freelance situation has actually been resolved for a while.
Would you say that all of your anxiety is directly related to your freelance business, or are there times when you feel anxious about other things?

Mostly it feels directly tied to the freelance business, yes. I mean, I came in because this all seemed to start getting out of hand when I tried to turn my art into an actual business instead of just something I did. That’s when I started getting really wound up over things like invoices, client messages, follow-ups, all of that.

And it’s not even always some huge crisis. It can be something as small as seeing an email from a client or knowing I need to send an invoice, and then I just… avoid it. I’ll tell myself I’m going to answer it after lunch, or after I make coffee, or once I’m “in the right headspace,” and then suddenly it’s been days and I’m sitting at my kitchen table crying because it feels so much bigger than it should.

There are probably other things I get anxious about, but the business stuff is the thing that seems to set everything off. When I’m tangled up in that, I start forgetting normal life stuff too, like paying a bill, because my brain is just stuck on the client messages or the invoice I haven’t dealt with. So I wouldn’t say I never feel anxious about anything else, but the freelance business is definitely the center of it.
Are there any times when you feel anxious about things that have nothing to do with your freelance business?

I mean, I’m trying to think of examples, and I’m sure I get normal worried about things here and there, but the anxiety that feels really out of proportion is almost always connected back to the freelance business somehow.

Like, I came in because ever since I tried to make my art into an actual business, instead of just something I did, I started getting so wound up over these very specific things — invoices, client messages, following up, anything where I feel like I have to be professional and keep everything moving. And then I avoid it, which makes it worse. I’ll see a message and think, “Okay, I’ll answer that in a bit,” and then I don’t, and then the longer I wait the more impossible it feels. Same with invoices. It’s not that the task itself is always huge, but in my head it becomes this whole mountain.

And then it spills over. I’ll be sitting at the kitchen table crying because I still haven’t answered someone or sent something, and then I realize I forgot some normal thing like paying a bill, not because I was anxious about the bill to begin with, but because my brain was so stuck on the business stuff.

So, no, I can’t really point to many times where it feels completely unrelated. It’s more like the freelance stress is the thing that starts it, and then it makes everything else harder.
Do you think your anxiety would persist even if the stressors related to your freelance business were completely removed?

I honestly don’t know, and that’s part of what makes it hard for me to answer clearly. The contract is still active, and the business changes are still sort of unfolding, so I haven’t really had a clean period where I could say, “Okay, the stressor is gone now, let’s see what happens.”

It’s not like everything ended and then I had several months to settle and could notice whether the anxiety stuck around on its own. I’m still dealing with the thing itself, and even the ripple effects from it are still there, so it feels like I’m trying to judge whether I’d be anxious without it while I’m still standing right in the middle of it.

So I guess my best answer is: maybe, but I can’t really tell yet. I’d need the freelance stuff to actually be resolved and have some time pass before I’d know whether the anxiety would keep going without that stressor.

Yeah, I think it probably would. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like my whole life would magically become perfect, but the anxiety I came in about feels really tied to that specific situation.

Ever since I tried to make my art into an actual freelance business — not just making things, but dealing with clients, invoices, messages, deadlines, all the “professional” parts — that’s when I started getting so wound up. Like I’ll see an email from a client or know I need to send an invoice, and instead of just doing it, I freeze and overthink it, and then I avoid it. And then the avoiding makes it worse, because suddenly it’s been days and now I’m convinced I’ve messed everything up.

So yeah, if I had a way to manage that part better — like not letting the invoices and messages turn into this huge scary thing — I think my anxiety would decrease a lot. Because it’s not like I’m anxious about everything equally. It’s more that this one area gets so overwhelming that it spills over, and then I’m crying at my kitchen table or forgetting basic normal things like paying a bill because I’m so stuck on what I haven’t dealt with for the business.

patient.answer:
There was a little bit of a gap, I think. It didn’t happen the exact day I said, “Okay, I’m doing freelance now.” At first I could kind of convince myself I was just figuring things out, and it felt manageable enough.

The part where I really started getting overwhelmed and avoidant was about a month after I took on the community arts contract and tried to make the business more formal. That’s when it stopped feeling like just making art or doing a few side jobs and started feeling like there were all these official responsibilities attached to it. And I think that shift really got to me.

So, yeah, there was maybe a short period where I was managing, or at least telling myself I was managing. But about a month into that more formal setup, that’s when I noticed I was freezing up and avoiding things instead of just handling them.

I mean, I came in because this all seemed to start getting out of hand when I tried to turn my art into an actual business instead of just something I did. I’ll tell myself I’m going to answer it after lunch, or after I make coffee, or once I’m “in the right headspace,” and then suddenly it’s been days and I’m sitting at my kitchen table crying because it feels so much bigger than it should.

There are probably other things I get anxious about, but the business stuff is the thing that seems to set everything off. When I’m tangled up in that, I start forgetting normal life stuff too, like paying a bill, because my brain is just stuck on the client messages or the invoice I haven’t dealt with. So I wouldn’t say I never feel anxious about anything else, but the freelance business is definitely the center of it.

Like, I came in because ever since I tried to make my art into an actual business, instead of just something I did, I started getting so wound up over these very specific things — invoices, client messages, following up, anything where I feel like I have to be professional and keep everything moving. And then I avoid it, which makes it worse. I’ll see a message and think, “Okay, I’ll answer that in a bit,” and then I don’t, and then the longer I wait the more impossible it feels. Same with invoices. It’s not that the task itself is always huge, but in my head it becomes this whole mountain.

And then it spills over. I’ll be sitting at the kitchen table crying because I still haven’t answered someone or sent something, and then I realize I forgot some normal thing like paying a bill, not because I was anxious about the bill to begin with, but because my brain was so stuck on the business stuff.

So, no, I can’t really point to many times where it feels completely unrelated. It’s more like the freelance stress is the thing that starts it, and then it makes everything else harder.
